readings.reading: A second topology τc : TopologicalSpace N, with ‹TopologicalSpace N› ≤ τc in mathlib's order, i.e. τc coarser, τc = τ allowed. C(W) is @connectedComponentIn N τc (p ⁻¹' W) x; the neighbourhood basis is in the topology of N. The general form drops τ ≤ τc and asks only hdiam. The component in N's own topology is the special case stronglyCausal_lift_self. In the intended instance M̃ is the maximal branched covering and τ = T_D = natural ∨ D*τ_X, which is mathlib's natural ⊓ TopologicalSpace.induced D τ_X. τc is the natural topology and hτ is inf_le_left.
readings.why: Components in a coarser topology are larger, so neither choice of τc implies the other's basis hypothesis. Taking τc as a parameter covers both.

readings.reading: Causal.Causality.StronglyCausal (DEC-7, neighbourhoods not necessarily open) for M, X and N. Checked both ways: with M and X StronglyCausalOpen, N is StronglyCausalOpen under the same hypotheses (stronglyCausalOpen_lift, stronglyCausalOpen_of_lift).
readings.why: the library's definition and its documented reading

readings.what: send causal curves to causal curves
readings.reading: The library has no such notion. Causal.WeakMorphism (Causal/Morphism.lean:161) is stronger: continuous, and locally monotone for ≤ and ≪. IsEMorphismOn.causalCurveOn_comp is stronger still. The theorems take the weakest form the proof uses: a causal curve of N (at U = ⊤) over [0, 1] goes to a causal curve of M (of X) at ⊤ over [0, 1]. Every other reading implies it. The refutation takes the strongest reading: any open U, any open U' ⊇ p(U), any segment. Weak morphisms enter through the new Causal.WeakMorphism.causalCurveOn_comp. The general form needs only monotonicity at M, ≤_N ⇒ ≤_M.
readings.why: dispatch: pick the weakest form the proof needs

readings.what: how ≤ of M̃ relates to its causal curves
readings.reading: Added: C.CausallyArcConnected, a ladder node. Of it the proof uses only the ≤ part at U = M, which is the hypothesis harc of mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves and le_top_map_of_curves. The general form uses only its consequence hdiam.
readings.why: The proof's first step treats the diamond J(a, b) as swept by causal curves. In ETT, ≤ is an abstract relation (defi:causalite), and without this hypothesis the statement is false (F1).

readings.reading: Filter.HasBasis (𝓝 x), indexed by the pairs (W, V) of open sets with p x ∈ W and D x ∈ V; the basis sets are C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V).

findings: F1, the printed form is false, in either reading of gluing (DEC-167). The hypothesis 'p and D send causal curves to causal curves' constrains ≤_M̃ only where ≤_M̃ is realised by causal curves, and the proof's first step ('a causal curve with ends in C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V)', programme/roadmap.toml:1953) assumes that it is. Refutation: Causal.not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves (StrongCausalityLifts.lean:647), with the curve hypothesis in its strongest reading. The witness is Causal.symmRationalLine (:512) on ℝ: x ≤_U y iff x = y ∈ U, or x and y are rational with the segment between them in U; ≪ is empty. It is absolutely minimal on every open set. Its causal curves are constant, so id into the timelike line sends each causal curve of any U to one in any U' ⊇ U. The timelike line is strongly causal, and the basis holds with the components in ℝ. Yet J(0, 0) ⊇ ℚ, so the space is not strongly causal; it is also not causally arc-connected (symmRationalLine_separates_lift, :629). The witness is not causal and not tarentin. Argued, not in Lean: an antisymmetric variant also works, so causality of M̃ does not rescue the statement. In it, x ≤_U y iff x = y ∈ U, or x and y are rational with φ x < φ y and the segment in U, for some φ : ℚ → ℝ that takes values in every open interval on every open interval.

F2: without gluing, weak morphisms and tarentin do not rescue either conclusion. Causal.not_alexandrovTopology_eq_lift_of_weakMorphism (:723), on timelikeLineTop with id, refutes 'C.StronglyCausal ∨ C.alexandrovTopology = τ'. timelikeLineTop is tarentin and id is a weak morphism; timelikeLineTop is not causal and not absolutely minimal (kb/0014, timelikeLineTop_separates_lift, :745). Under gluing, the tarentin half of the printed form is neither proved nor refuted without causal arc-connectedness.

F3 (positive), the strongest true form proved. With N causally arc-connected, the target holds as stated: Causal.Causality.stronglyCausal_lift (:332), and alexandrovTopology_eq_lift (:347) for the tarentin conclusion. More generally, stronglyCausal_of_lift (:220) needs neither curves nor τ ≤ τc nor continuity. It asks that p and D be monotone for ≤ at M, and hdiam: every diamond J_N(a, z) has a τc-preconnected subset through a and z. rationalLine_strongCausalityLift_top (:481) applies it to the rational line, which is not causally arc-connected, with the indiscrete τc.

F4 (positive): the open form costs nothing more. With M and X StronglyCausalOpen, N is StronglyCausalOpen under the same hypotheses (stronglyCausalOpen_lift, :360). Under the basis hypothesis every C(W) ∩ D⁻¹(V) with W and V open is open, because it is the basis set of each of its points (isOpen_connectedComponentIn_inter_preimage, :197).

F5: under gluing, weak morphisms are automatically monotone at M (Causal.WeakMorphism.le_top_of_absolutelyMinimal, :134), so stronglyCausal_of_lift_of_weakMorphism (:312) reduces the remaining gap to hdiam alone.
questions: Q1: is M̃'s causality meant to be the causality of its causal curves (causally arc-connected)? It is in the intended instance: ETT's causality from curves on (M̃, T_D), DEC-33. Reading taken: yes. It is added as C.CausallyArcConnected in the target's form; the general form asks only hdiam. Without some such hypothesis the statement is false (F1).

Q2 (open): under gluing (DEC-167), with p and D weak morphisms rather than maps that only send curves to curves, is hdiam, or causal arc-connectedness, still needed? Without gluing it is (F2). Under gluing I found neither a proof nor a counterexample. Absolute minimality gives monotone maps (F5), but chains of local links can jump between components of p⁻¹(W) near its boundary.
Q3: 'the coarser topology' was read as any τc coarser than M̃'s topology, τc = τ allowed (stronglyCausal_lift_self). The intended τc is the natural topology of the branched covering.

Q4, for the instantiating closers (T-loc-btz-tamifying-initial, T-loc-ealpha-tamifying-alexandrov): grep found no proof of CausallyArcConnected for lean-gx's GX.btzCylCausality. The instance needs either that, or the weaker harc (≤_⊤ realised by causal curves of ⊤ over [0, 1]), which is what mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves takes. GX.btzCylCausality_le_top_iff (globally ≤ is the order of the developments) may give it. Alternatively, it needs hdiam directly.

kb_proposals: Two topologies on one type in a statement: an explicit binder (τc : TopologicalSpace N) is still a local instance, and the most recent one wins. Bind it BEFORE [TopologicalSpace N] so that the causality's ⊤, diamonds and curves use the ambient topology. Pass τc only through @ (@connectedComponentIn N τc …). In @ mode the binder ⦃a⦄ of a ⊆ conclusion is explicit: write (@lemma … h₁ h₂) hmem. #check prints connectedComponentIn without its instance (T-abs-strong-causality-lifts).

Causal.symmRationalLine: on ℝ, two rationals are related both ways when their segment lies in U. It is absolutely minimal on every open set (from rationalLine_absolutelyMinimalOn and TransGen.swap), its causal curves are constant, and it is not strongly causal. It refutes, in either gluing reading, any statement whose hypotheses read only causal curves but whose conclusion reads ≤ (T-abs-strong-causality-lifts).

A weak morphism out of an absolutely minimal causality is monotone at M (Causal.WeakMorphism.le_top_of_absolutelyMinimal). Weak morphisms send causal curves of V to causal curves of every open U ⊇ φ(V) (Causal.WeakMorphism.causalCurveOn_comp).

In the indiscrete topology every set is preconnected and connectedComponentIn F x = F (Causal.isPreconnected_top, Causal.connectedComponentIn_top). It is a free coarse topology for statements about components.
`MapsTo id U U'` with U U' : Opens ℝ fails to elaborate, because the coercion to Set needs id's type. Write (id : ℝ → ℝ).
